surfaces.part: lower cabinet with red seat cushion

answer.evidence: This is an arcade cabinet, not a container with an opening. The only opening is a dark recess in the lower body, and it is seen face-on. The top marquee band (rows 1-5) shades from dark red to a light front-edge line at row 5, with dark eave shadow in rows 6-7. That meets evidence (a), but it is a thin band, and it could instead be a face-on marquee. The wider control panel (rows 20-28) has a lighter line at row 24 and a joystick ellipse. The screen (rows 8-18) is a vertical face. The lower body (rows 29-46) is a vertical face of about 18 rows with a red cushion. The overall front face is roughly 39 rows. There is no receding side face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The cabinet reads clearly as a red arcade machine with a screen, but its shading is shallow. The red body has about 3 steps (a light red, a mid red and a dark red) and the panel and base are mostly one tone each. The outline is a uniform dark line around the whole silhouette. The measured 100% near-neutral share of dark edge pixels confirms it is neutral black or grey rather than a tinted dark material tone. That is the sticker look, while the Beodeul stall and well references have tinted outlines at 1% and 33% neutral. Texture is minimal: the body is smooth with no grain, speckle or per-surface highlights, though the 6% near-flat coverage shows few large flat blocks. The candidate has 16 visible tones per tile against 17 for the stall and 20 for the well, so density is only slightly lower. The tone count is partly inflated by the screen and the control details, not by material texture. Next to the references, the near-black outline and the few shading steps make it look flatter and more sticker-like.

The structure is clean and readable, but it is flatter and more sticker-like than the references next to it.

The screen and bezel (rows 8-18) and the lower body with seat and pedal (rows 29-46) are vertical front faces, giving a front face of about 39 rows. The wider control panel (28 vs 26 px, rows 20-24) has its own lighter band ending in an edge line at row 24, then red front rows 25-28, so it also reads as a protruding horizontal surface. answer.evidence: The cabinet is drawn as a flat front view. The marquee (rows 1-7) is a front-facing sign strip with a highlight row at 5 and a dark row at 6-7, so it reads as a shaded face rather than a roof. The screen (rows 8-18) is a vertical face. The control deck (rows 20-28) is a rounded horizontal bar that looks like a cylinder, with no clear receding top plane. Rows 29-43 show a front view of a dark lower cabin with a red seat and a gray base strip at rows 44-45. No ellipse, open mouth or visible contents of a container appear anywhere, and the object is not a container. The silhouette widens from 26 to 28 at rows 20-29 and returns to 24, which is only the deck sticking out sideways.

styleAnswer.evidence: Tile density holds up: 16 visible tones per tile against 17-20 for the stall and well, and only 6% near-flat coverage, so there are no large flat fills. The structure is the weak point. The red cabinet body and the dark side panels read as about 3 lightness steps each, where Beodeul materials use 5-6. All of the candidate's dark edge pixels are near-neutral (100%), so the outline is a uniform black/grey line around the whole cabinet. That is the sticker look. The stall, hedge and well references use tinted outlines (0-33% neutral), which is what the candidate lacks. The screen and buttons add small tonal variety but not the per-material ramps or grain the references show. A careful artist would see the black outline and shallow ramps as below the Beodeul bar next to the stall and well.
